date.note: Online publication date on the Nature article page.

key_value_text.quote: The solar pp neutrino interaction rate measured by Borexino is 144 ± 13 (stat.) ± 10 (syst.) c.p.d. per 100 t.
key_value_text.value: pp neutrino interaction rate 144 ± 13 (stat) ± 10 (syst) counts per day per 100 t

name: Neutrinos from the primary proton–proton fusion process in the Sun
notes: Classified as a measurement rather than a discovery, observation, evidence or first-detection claim: the paper's title makes no such claim. The abstract's own wording is 'spectral observations of pp neutrinos' that had 'hitherto eluded direct detection'.

significance.quote: The absence of pp solar neutrinos is excluded with a statistical significance of 10σ
significance.value: 10σ (absence of pp solar neutrinos excluded; statistical significance)

summary.plain: Borexino reported spectral observations of the Sun's most abundant neutrinos, the pp neutrinos from the very first step of the fusion chain that powers it, which the paper says had hitherto eluded direct detection.
summary.technical: Spectral observations of pp neutrinos with the Borexino liquid-scintillator detector at LNGS: pp neutrino interaction rate 144 ± 13 (stat) ± 10 (syst) counts per day per 100 t, flux (6.6 ± 0.7) × 10¹⁰ cm⁻² s⁻¹ in good agreement with the standard solar model prediction; the absence of pp neutrinos is excluded with a statistical significance of 10σ, and about 99% of the Sun's power (3.84 × 10³³ erg/s) is generated by proton–proton fusion.

title: Neutrinos from the primary proton–proton fusion process in the Sun

why_it_matters.quote: These so-called pp neutrinos constitute nearly the entirety of the solar neutrino flux ... Spectral observations of the low-energy neutrinos produced by proton–proton fusion in the Sun demonstrate that about 99 per cent of the Sun’s power is generated by this process.
why_it_matters.value: Direct spectral observation of the pp neutrinos, which make up nearly the entirety of the solar neutrino flux and had hitherto eluded direct detection, demonstrating that about 99 per cent of the Sun's power is generated by proton-proton fusion.
